mainKeyword: all in one washer dryer combos
metaDescription: Six single-drum washer dryer combos for apartments and RVs, compared on dry capacity, venting, drain needs, spin speed and the cycle times they really take.
expertTake: The Midea 2.7 cu ft ventless combo is the best match for most apartments, with a 1400 RPM spin that shortens the dry stage. The Hamilton Beach is the pick when you want published wash and dry capacities to plan loads by. If you do laundry for a family of five, a stacked pair will beat any combo, because a single drum always does one job at a time.
introParagraphs: A washer dryer combo washes and dries in one drum, so it fits where a stacked pair will not. The trade is time and capacity: it only handles one load at once, and the drying half is far smaller and slower than the washing half.

Most of these machines condense moisture instead of venting it outside, which is why they run from a normal outlet and need no duct. That convenience is the whole reason to buy one, and also the reason a dry cycle takes hours.

products.name: Midea 2.7 cu ft 24 in ventless combo, 1400 RPM

specList.label: Special cycles
specList.value: Steam care, overnight wash and dry

products.description:
The Midea is a 24 inch front-loader with a 2.7 cu ft drum and a 1400 RPM spin, and the spin speed is the spec that matters most for a combo. A faster spin wrings more water from the load before the dry stage, so the slow, ventless drying has less to do. The listing positions it for households of three to four.

It dries by condensation with no vent, so it needs only a water supply, a drain and an outlet. There is an overnight wash and dry cycle for starting a load before bed and waking up to dry clothes, and a steam care option for refreshing garments. Remember that steam is not a stain remedy on its own.

Compared with the COMFEE below, it is the better choice when you want the higher spin speed on the listing. Compared with the Hamilton Beach, it lacks published dry capacity, so plan on a dry load noticeably smaller than the wash load and avoid overfilling. Level the four feet and remove the transit bolts before the first cycle.
products.bestFor: Apartments for two to four people with no vent.
pros: 1400 RPM spin shortens the dry stage
Ventless, so no duct is needed
cons: Dry capacity is much smaller than wash capacity
Needs a drain and a cold water tap

products.name: Hamilton Beach 2.65 cu ft combo, 26.4 lb wash and 17.6 lb dry
products.description:
Hamilton Beach publishes both capacities, 26.4 lb for washing and 17.6 lb for drying, and that is the most useful number on any combo listing. It tells you a full wash load will not dry in one go, so you split or remove items rather than finding damp laundry at the end.

The front-load unit offers four temperature settings from extra hot to cold and more than a dozen cycles, which is a larger menu than most compacts. Because it is a ventless combo, drying uses condensation and can take two to four hours for a load, so plan for that rather than expecting a standard dryer's speed.

Compared with the Midea, it gives you better information for planning and a similar drum size. Compared with the Equator, it carries nearly twice the dry capacity of a 15 lb unit. Check the drain height and hose length against your standpipe before you order, since a drain placed too low or high causes leaks and siphoning.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want to size loads by real numbers.
pros: Publishes both wash and dry capacities
2.65 cu ft drum suits small families
cons: Dry load is about two thirds of the wash load
Needs a drain at the right height

products.name: Equator 24 in 110V convertible combo, 1.6 cu ft, 1400 RPM
products.description:
The Equator is the smaller, convertible option: a 1.62 cu ft, 15 lb drum that can dry either vented for faster performance or ventless where no duct exists. The choice matters because vented drying is quicker, and you only get that benefit if you have a place to run the vent.

It spins at 1400 RPM, which matches the Midea, and adds a pet cycle designed to remove embedded hair before drying starts. For a household with dogs or cats, that cycle spares the dry stage from baking hair into fabric. It runs from a 110V outlet, like most compact units.

The small drum is the tradeoff. At 15 lb it suits one or two people, not a family, and the dry capacity will be smaller still. Compared with the Splendide, it is a household unit rather than an RV unit, and compared with the Midea it costs less per load but handles less. Decide on the vent at purchase, because switching later means extra parts.
products.bestFor: One or two people, especially with pets.
pros: Choice of vented or ventless drying
cons: Vented mode needs a duct run

products.name: Splendide vented 15 lb combo with vent kit
products.description:
The Splendide is built around RV living, where a closet and an exterior wall are the install location. It is a vented 15 lb combo that comes with a complete vent kit, so you run the exhaust through the wall and dry faster than a condensing unit can. Making the duct run is the install job to plan for.

A dual-rotating drum and variable spin speeds reduce wrinkles and help the drying, according to the listing. The unit is compact and is meant for the fresh water and gray tank limits of an RV, so check your capacity, because washers on HE settings use roughly 10 to 20 gallons a cycle.

Compared with the Equator, it is a vented unit rather than a convertible one. Compared with the Contoure, it dries faster but demands the vent run. Its 15 lb size suits one or two people, and the 120V supply and your RV's electrical system need checking, because heated drying draws a lot of current.
products.bestFor: RV owners with an exterior wall for a vent.
cons: Needs a vent run through a wall
Uses fresh water on every cycle

products.name: Contoure 2.7 cu ft ventless combo with steam, 120V
products.description:
The Contoure is a 2.7 cu ft ventless combo that the listing positions for both RV and residential use, with 120V operation so it plugs into ordinary power. Being ventless, it needs no exterior wall, which makes it the easier install when the washer closet is in the middle of the vehicle or the apartment.

A steam function helps reduce wrinkles and refresh garments, though as with all steam cycles it is a refresher, not a stain treatment. The larger 2.7 cu ft drum gives it more capacity than the 15 lb RV units, but it dries by condensation, so expect long cycles and a smaller dry load.

Against the Splendide, it trades faster vented drying for installation flexibility. Against the Midea, it is aimed more at RV buyers, so check water and drain details in the manual. Mind the weight: these machines run 150 to 200 lb, which matters on a floor with limited support.
products.bestFor: RVs or apartments without a place to vent.
pros: Ventless install with no wall penetration
cons: Dry load much smaller than wash load

products.name: COMFEE 24 in 2.7 cu ft combo, 26 lb, steam and overnight dry

specList.label: Cycles
specList.value: Steam care, overnight wash and dry

products.description:
The COMFEE is the budget-friendly 24 inch combo with a 26 lb wash capacity, steam care and an overnight wash and dry cycle. The listing highlights a design aimed at reducing shaking, which is a real concern because a front-loader with a high spin can walk across the floor if it is not level.

Its ventless drying follows the standard condensing approach, with a cold water supply for the condenser and a drain, and dry loads are much smaller than wash loads. The 26 lb figure is the wash capacity, so treat dry capacity as around two thirds of it.

Compared with the Midea, it carries a similar drum and the same feature set, and the difference comes down to price and which spin speed the listing states. Compared with the Hamilton Beach, it does not publish a dry capacity. Use HE detergent, leave the door ajar after each wash and wipe the door seal to avoid the mildew smell front-loaders develop.
products.bestFor: Budget buyers who want 26 lb wash capacity.
cons: Requires HE detergent and door care

buyingCriteria.criterion: Read dry capacity, not wash capacity
buyingCriteria.explanation: Combos wash more than they dry. The Hamilton Beach lists 26.4 lb for washing and 17.6 lb for drying, and the Equator is 15 lb overall. Overfilling the dry stage leaves clothes damp. If you wash a full drum, plan to remove a third before drying or run a second cycle.

Ventless units like the Midea and Contoure condense moisture and need no duct, but take two to four hours per load. Vented units like the Splendide dry faster but need an exterior wall and a vent kit. The Equator can do either. Choose by what your space allows, not by the spec sheet.

A 1400 RPM spin, as on the Midea and Equator, extracts more water than a slower spin, which cuts drying time. Higher spin raises vibration, so floor stiffness matters. A combo on a wood floor can walk or hum if it is not leveled.

Most 24 inch machines need a cold water hookup and a standpipe or drain at roughly 30 to 36 inches height. Ventless units use water for condensing as well. Look at the manual for the drain height and hose length before buying, because a mismatch causes leaks.

All of these run from 110 to 120V, which suits a normal 15 to 20 amp circuit. Heated dry cycles may draw 10 amps or more, so do not share the circuit with a microwave or space heater. In an RV, check the shore power and the breaker rating.

Combos weigh 150 to 200 lb, so floor support matters, especially in an RV. New front-loaders need the transit bolts removed, and the four feet leveled to reduce walking and noise. Skipping either step is the most common first-week problem.

specDecoder.meaning: Combos list a wash capacity in pounds that is larger than the dry capacity. The dry figure is the real working limit.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Hamilton Beach lists 26.4 lb and 17.6 lb, which is the clearest example.

specDecoder.meaning: Moist air is cooled by cold water so it condenses and drains away, rather than being exhausted outside.
specDecoder.watchFor: Expect cycles of two to four hours, and make sure a cold water tap is connected.

specDecoder.meaning: Spin speed in revolutions per minute. Higher speeds extract more water and shorten drying.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Midea and Equator list 1400 RPM; confirm floor strength for the vibration.

specDecoder.meaning: A design that can dry vented for speed or ventless for flexibility.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Equator offers it, and switching modes needs the right parts.

specDecoder.meaning: A cycle that injects steam to relax wrinkles and refresh fabrics.
specDecoder.watchFor: Steam helps with refreshing, not with stains, on the Midea, COMFEE and Contoure.

howWeEvaluated.title: Dry capacity honesty
howWeEvaluated.description: We favored listings that publish a dry capacity. The Hamilton Beach gives 17.6 lb dry against 26.4 lb wash, while others list one figure and leave the real dry limit unclear.

howWeEvaluated.title: Venting flexibility
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared ventless, vented and convertible designs. The Equator is convertible, the Splendide is vented with a kit and the Midea and Contoure are ventless.

howWeEvaluated.title: Spin and floor impact
howWeEvaluated.description: We noted spin speeds such as 1400 RPM and considered how they affect drying time and vibration. Higher spin helps drying but wants a stiff floor.

howWeEvaluated.title: Install requirements
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at water, drain, vent and power needs. Ventless units need a cold tap and a drain, and the Splendide needs a wall vent.

howWeEvaluated.title: Size for the household
howWeEvaluated.description: We matched drum sizes to household sizes. The 15 lb units suit one or two people and the 2.7 cu ft units suit three to four.

cards.label: Ventless
cards.text: The Midea, COMFEE, Hamilton Beach and Contoure condense moisture and need no duct. Install is easy, but cycles take two to four hours and dry loads are small.

cards.label: Vented
cards.text: The Splendide, and the Equator in vented mode, exhaust moist air outside. Drying is faster, but you need an exterior wall and a vent run.

howToChoose.note: Choose ventless if you cannot vent; choose vented if you have a wall and want speed.

howToChoose.subheading: For Apartments and Tiny Homes Specifically

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A 24 inch width, a ventless dry stage, a spin of 1200 RPM or more and clear drain requirements. Check that the floor and drain at your location suit a 150 to 200 lb machine.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Midea and Hamilton Beach both suit an apartment closet. The Hamilton Beach gives better load planning and the Midea gives a higher spin speed.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You need vented speed or a particular install. The Splendide gives faster drying in an RV and the Equator gives flexibility in an apartment you may leave.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You will run one load at a time and have time to spare. The COMFEE and Hamilton Beach give a 2.7 cu ft drum at the lower end of the range.

maintenance.why: Moisture and detergent collect in the boot and breed mildew. Leave the door ajar to dry.
A hot empty cycle with a washer cleaner removes residue from the drum and drain path.
Lint blocks airflow and lengthens dry cycles, which are already long on a ventless machine.
Leaks usually come from loose drain clamps or a failed door boot. A quick inspection prevents floor damage.
Vibration shifts the machine over time. A level drum runs quieter and walks less.

faq.q: Why does the dry cycle take so long?
faq.a: Ventless combos condense moisture with cold water instead of exhausting it, so a load takes two to four hours. A higher spin speed and a smaller dry load shorten it.

faq.q: Can I wash and dry a full load?
faq.a: Usually not. Dry capacity is smaller than wash capacity, as the Hamilton Beach's 26.4 lb wash and 17.6 lb dry show. Remove about a third or run two dry cycles.
Not for ventless models like the Midea or Contoure. The Splendide needs one, and the Equator can use one for faster drying. Choose by your space.

faq.q: Will it fit a standard outlet?
faq.a: Yes. They run on 110 to 120V, but heated dry cycles may draw 10 amps or more, so avoid sharing the circuit with other heavy appliances.

faq.q: Is a combo better than a stacked pair?
faq.a: Only where space is the constraint. A combo handles one load at a time, and a stacked pair washes and dries at once. For larger families, the pair is faster.

faq.q: How do I stop the musty smell?
faq.a: Use HE detergent, wipe the door seal and leave the door ajar between loads. Run a monthly cleaning cycle to clear residue from the drum.
